key_insight: FracLearn teaches a language model to improve physical design decisions by turning simulated fracture experiences into reusable principles for better architecture generation.
engineering_relevance: The framework suggests a path for materials and structural design agents that learn from experiments without retraining model weights, potentially speeding discovery of tougher, more efficient designs.
method: Generate candidate architectures in a fracture-based game environment.
Observe simulated fracture responses and abstract them into conditional design principles.
Generalize those principles to new designs and revise hypotheses through repeated campaigns.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the best composite score exceeded the experience-stage record by 11.0%, with fracture analysis linking gains to crack deflection, temporary trapping, and higher residual load capacity.
watch_item: Results come from a deliberately unfamiliar game-like simulator, so transfer to real materials systems may require careful validation.
paper_title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
